newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi visit to France political, not military.
newsitem.headline: Saudi visit to France political, not military.

text.p: A visit to Paris by Saudi Arabia's Defence and Aviation Minister Prince Sultan on Wednesday will boost already strong political, economic, military and security ties, Western diplomats said on Tuesday.
But the prince, also second deputy prime minister, is not expected to sign any military deals during the three-day visit, they said.
"Prince Sultan's visit is a political one, not a military one," a French diplomatic source in Saudi Arabia told Reuters. "The Saudis insist they are not coming to sign any military contract."
France is trying to convince Saudi Arabia to buy Leclerq main battle tanks made by Giat Industries, similar to those sold for $3.62 billion to neighbouring United Arab Emirates in 1993.
It is competing with Britain and the United States for the major arms contract after its tanks were tested in the kingdom's desert this summer at Saudi Arabia's request.
Diplomats had said France also hoped to turn a memorandum of understanding on radar and surveillance systems for zone and border defence into contracts.
Prince Sultan, who visited Washington last week, is expected to meet French President Jacques Chirac, Prime Minister Alain Juppe, Defence Minister Charles Millon and other officials.
"The French government will receive him more as Saudi Arabia's second deputy prime minister than its defence minister," another French diplomat said.
"Military cooperation will be one of the many subjects that will be raised in the talks that will also cover regional developments...the situation in Iraq and the Arab-Israeli peace process."
But Paris, seeking to enhance its political role in the region, still hopes to promote military and commercial trade with the world's biggest arms purchaser.

France, which buys one-quarter of its oil from Saudi Arabia, is the kingdom's third biggest arms supplier after the United States and Britain. Weapons sales average $1.2 billion a year, roughly equivalent to civilian exports.
Chirac saw Saudi King Fahd in Riyadh last July and both said their talks consolidated and ensured continued cooperation on all levels.
France took part in a U.S.-led Western military alliance that drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War.
Diplomats said talks held by French armed forces chief General Jean-Philippe Douin and his Saudi Arabian counterpart Saleh al-Muhaya in Riyadh on Monday had no connection with Prince Sultan's visit.
"They discussed routine military cooperation and General Douin attended the opening session of the annual meetings of the joint Saudi-French military commission," one said.
